task.description:
Perform WF-02 Step 5 (release validation) for REQ-373 per docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md. Independently RE-RUN scripts/test_parallel.sh yourself -- do not trust TEST-RUNNER's report alone; run it synchronously in the foreground (per core-directives.md's 'No Background Wait For A Cross-Turn Notification' -- this applies to you specifically). Your re-run will not reproduce Step 4's exact result and that is expected; do not treat a differing count as confirmation or regression -- attribute any failure structurally yourself, do not accept Step 4's attributions on its say-so.

Confirm every one of REQ-373's 8 acceptance criteria is satisfied -- check each one explicitly against the actual code/test, not against any prior step's summary: (1) version identity + ACTIVE/RETIRED status with schema decision + reasoning in moduledoc, migration + schema test; (2) publish doesn't disturb an already-resolved pin, proven by test; (3) new case after publish resolves the new version via the real Lookup, proven by test; (4) retire is two-sided (fails new resolution, pin_for/3 unaffected), proven by test; (5) Engine.create/2's pin_lookup/2 wired to real Lookup for catalog_entry, proven by integration test; (6) publish/retire gated by :AdminServicesManage, no new permission, proven by test; (7) PLC-01/module_ref explicitly out of scope in moduledoc with citation; (8) mix letflow.check passes, real output quoted. Also run `mix letflow.check` yourself and quote the real output as part of AC8's own verification.

Check docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (via the index) and docs/requirements.yaml for staleness relative to what actually shipped -- confirm REQ-373 is still correctly `in_progress` (not yet flipped to done, that's DOC-UPDATER's job next) and that the started event already recorded matches what actually shipped. Complete the handoff with PASS -> 'Route to DOC-UPDATER' or FAIL naming the blocking issue and which agent it routes back to. Commit and push (explicit filenames, never -A) before ending your turn.
acceptance_criteria: service_catalog entries carry a version identity and an ACTIVE/RETIRED status, with the chosen schema stated explicitly in the moduledoc along with the reasoning, proven by a migration and a schema test
publishing a new version of an existing service_id does not alter or invalidate any already-resolved pinned_version entry recorded in a prior INSTANCE_STARTED event, proven by a test
a new case created after a publish resolves the newly published version via PinResolver.resolve/4's real Lookup, proven by a test

retiring a version prevents any NEW resolution from choosing it while an instance already pinned to the retired version continues to resolve via pin_for/3 with no error, proven by a test covering both sides
Engine.create/2's pin_lookup/2 helper is wired to the real catalog-backed Lookup for catalog_entry references, proven by an integration test
publish/retire operations are gated behind :AdminServicesManage, not a newly invented permission name, proven by a test
PLC-01/module_ref catalog versioning is explicitly named as still out of scope in the moduledoc, citing pin_resolver.ex's own SCOPE GAP language
mix letflow.check passes, with real output quoted

ac_verification.AC1: PASS -- lib/letflow/service_catalog/entry.ex declares version/version_id/status(Ecto.Enum :ACTIVE|:RETIRED)/published_at/retired_at; lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex moduledoc states the schema decision (in-place columns + sibling service_catalog_versions archive table, not composite-key) with full reasoning verbatim; priv/repo/migrations/20260921000003_add_service_catalog_versioning.exs adds the columns + CHECK constraint + archive table; test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs 'REQ-373 AC1' describe block covers the stamped-defaults case and a DB-level CHECK-violation case, both re-read and confirmed present and correctly asserting.
ac_verification.AC2: PASS -- ServiceCatalog.publish/3's own @doc/moduledoc states the 'zero EventStore I/O' invariant explicitly; test/letflow/engine_pin_resolver_catalog_test.exs 'REQ-373 AC2' starts a real Engine.create/2 instance, publishes a new version of the same service_id, then re-derives the SAME instance's pin set via PinResolver.reconstruct_effective_pins/2 and asserts version/resolved_id are UNCHANGED (still "1"/entry.version_id, not the newly published "2").
ac_verification.AC3: PASS -- lib/letflow/service_catalog/pin_lookup.ex's catalog_lookup/1 resolves the live ACTIVE row's version_id/version; test/letflow/engine_pin_resolver_catalog_test.exs 'REQ-373 AC3' publishes a new version then calls PinResolver.resolve/4 with PinLookup.build/0 directly and asserts the returned pin's version/resolved_id/source(:resolved) match the NEW version, not the original.
ac_verification.AC4: PASS, both sides in one test -- ServiceCatalog.retire/1's @doc states the 'fails outright, never falls through' decision with reasoning (structural: at most one live row per service_id); PinLookup.catalog_lookup/1 maps a RETIRED row to {:error, :not_found}, which resolve/4 turns into the EXISTING {:error, {:unresolved_catalog_ref, ref}} variant (no new error atom). test/letflow/engine_pin_resolver_catalog_test.exs 'REQ-373 AC4' captures a pin BEFORE retire, retires, then asserts (a) a FRESH resolve/4 call fails with :unresolved_catalog_ref and (b) PinResolver.pin_for/3 over the pre-retire pin still returns {:ok, pin} unchanged -- both halves in the same test function, sharing one service_id, as the design/spec called for.
ac_verification.AC5: PASS -- lib/letflow/engine.ex:990-992's pin_lookup/2 now reads Map.get(attrs, :pin_lookup, PinLookup.build()) in place of PinResolver.default_lookup(); confirmed by direct read of the current call site (not the design doc's description of it). test/letflow/engine_pin_resolver_catalog_test.exs 'REQ-373 AC5' calls Engine.create/2 with NO :pin_lookup override and asserts the recorded INSTANCE_STARTED pin has source: "resolved" (not the old unconditional :unresolved_catalog_ref failure), plus a companion test confirming an unregistered service_id still fails identically to before this wiring.
ac_verification.AC6: PASS -- lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex declares both new routes (`authz_post "/:service_id/versions", :AdminServicesManage` and `authz_post "/:service_id/retire", :AdminServicesManage`) using the already-shipped policy key; confirmed no lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex diff (git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD does not list it) and SECURITY-REVIEWER's own handoff (step-02c) independently re-derived the same conclusion by reading AuthorizedRouter's authz_post/3 macro and re-running test/letflow/api/authorization_enforcement_test.exs. test/letflow/routers/admin_services_publish_retire_test.exs proves both halves for both routes: 403 + untouched row for a non-PLATFORM_ADMIN caller (including a no-roles-at-all case), 201/200 + real state transition for PLATFORM_ADMIN.
ac_verification.AC7: PASS -- lib/letflow/service_catalog/pin_lookup.ex's moduledoc and lib/letflow/service_catalog/entry.ex's moduledoc both explicitly cite pin_resolver.ex's own 'SCOPE GAP -- service_catalog (S6) and PLC-01 (unscoped) are not built' section by name; PinLookup.build/0's module_lookup field is copied verbatim from PinResolver.default_lookup/0 (a permanent {:error, :not_found} stub), never reimplemented -- confirmed by direct source read.
ac_verification.AC8: PASS -- mix letflow.check run independently by RELEASE-VALIDATOR, real output quoted below, exit 0.

This is a pre-existing, environmental, correctly-attributed non-regression; it is not filed as a new issue since ISS-0110 already covers the exact mechanism -- flagging here per 'A failure not covered by an existing issue record is called out as such' (it IS covered).
